source_user: A sparse MoE service has uneven expert load and tail latency. Analyze likely causes and experiments. Scenario variant 179: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure routing distribution, expert capacity overflow, all-to-all time, token dropping/padding, placement, batch composition, and compare routing/capacity policies.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the router uses top-k sparse dispatch; expert capacity, routing, placement, batching, and admission are configurable; clocks can be synchronized; and model weights and quality tests are held fixed. The observed load skew and tail are not proof of causality.

Likely causes are concentrated router assignments or correlated inputs, insufficient capacity causing overflow/dropped or padded tokens, expert queueing or compute imbalance, cross-device all-to-all contention, poor expert-to-GPU/NIC/NUMA locality, batch-shape and admission-burst effects, retries, and unrelated CPU, network, thermal, or scheduler interference. Hypothesis: if hot-expert concentration or remote communication is causal, reducing routing skew or improving locality/capacity will lower p95/p99 end-to-end latency and queue time while preserving output correctness and a predeclared token-loss/quality budget; if not, those metrics will not improve in matched trials.

Measure, with units and synchronized timestamps, per request/batch/expert/device: routed-token counts and fractions, top-k probabilities/entropy, max/mean load and coefficient of variation, capacity factor, overflow/dropped/padded tokens, queue, dispatch, expert compute, combine, and all-to-all durations, bytes and retries, expert placement and locality, batch size/sequence lengths, concurrency, GPU utilization/memory, network counters, errors, and p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput and quality/correctness. Trace token identity or checksums to detect loss/duplication.

Run a randomized blocked experiment over representative length, arrival-rate, and tenant strata. Compare the baseline with one-factor-at-a-time and factorial variants for routing balancing/top-k policy, capacity factor, expert placement/locality, and batch/admission limits; include single-device/no-all-to-all and synthetic balanced-routing controls. Warm up, repeat enough trials for confidence intervals, and predeclare a practical p99 improvement and zero-tolerance correctness/token-loss gate. Avoid confounding routing, capacity, placement, and batch changes in one conclusion; control software version, model, hardware, seeds, traffic, thermal state, and background load.

Use a bounded shadow or canary, cap concurrency and capacity, preserve a known-good configuration, and roll back on errors, token loss/duplication, quality regression, saturation, or SLO breach. Do not claim a root cause from correlations or a single workload. Evidence required: synchronized traces and per-expert counters, repeated matched results with uncertainty, correctness/quality checks, and confirmation that the intervention—not altered traffic or hidden overflow—caused the change.

Assumptions: draft and target models share the tokenizer and compatible output semantics, verification is exact or uses a specified acceptance rule, and timings are measured on the same hardware/software and workload. A slower speculative decoder can result from draft work, target verification, synchronization, transfers, low acceptance, or batching effects; the target-only baseline is required.

Hypothesis: speculation is beneficial only when the expected accepted tokens per target verification step times target-only per-token cost exceeds draft, verification, transfer, and synchronization overhead. Measure end-to-end latency, TTFT/TPOT, p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost, and GPU utilization for target-only and speculative modes under matched prompt-length, output-length, concurrency, and arrival-rate strata.

Instrument draft latency per step and token, target verification latency and batch size, acceptance rate by position and by workload, accepted tokens per step, rejected-token recomputation, target calls, synchronization/barrier and CPU scheduling time, logits/KV-cache transfer bytes and time, memory pressure, queueing, and power/cost. Check output equivalence, token accounting, and any quality impact. Use synchronized traces rather than summed wall-clock components without overlap accounting.

Run randomized paired trials with warmed caches and repeated seeds across draft models, speculation lengths, concurrency, and workload strata; include target-only, a no-transfer/control where meaningful, and fixed-batch controls. Predeclare a break-even throughput/latency threshold and confidence intervals. Control versions, precision, kernels, hardware clocks, thermal state, batching policy, scheduler, and prompt/output distributions.

Canary only within a bounded traffic fraction with a feature flag, resource cap, target-only fallback, and rollback on correctness mismatch, acceptance collapse, memory/SLO breach, error increase, or negative cost-adjusted latency. Evidence required before rollout: paired measurements with uncertainty, position-wise acceptance and overhead decomposition, reproducible target-only comparison, and correctness/quality validation; do not infer that a low acceptance rate alone explains the slowdown if queueing or transfer overlap is unmeasured.

quality_dimensions.coverage: explicit assumptions, mechanisms, boundaries, measurements, experiments, confounders, safety and rollback
quality_dimensions.mechanism_reasoning: causal hypotheses are separated from observations and tested with matched controls
quality_dimensions.measurement_plan: per-request/expert/device traces with units, uncertainty, correctness and quality checks
quality_dimensions.failure_handling: bounded canary, fallback, predeclared gates and rollback

risks: correlation may be mistaken for causation
instrumentation can perturb tail latency
unmeasured token loss or output mismatch can invalidate comparisons
evidence_required: synchronized traces and baseline/control measurements
repeated randomized matched trials with confidence intervals
correctness/quality and SLO checks before rollout
